'''Stratasys, Ltd.''' is an American-Israeli manufacturer of [[3D printer]]s, software, and materials for polymer [[additive manufacturing]] as well as 3D-printed parts on-demand.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Engle |first1=Greg |title=Hot Off The Press: Nascar Teams With Stratasys For 3D-Printed Parts |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/gregengle/2022/06/01/hot-off-the-press-nascar-teams-with-stratasys-for-3d-printed-parts/?sh=2c23ae8c7270 |website=[[Forbes]] |date=June 1, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Lessons from the Greatest Stock Traders of All Time |last=Boik |first=John |year=2004 |publisher=McGraw-Hill Professional |isbn=978-0-07-143788-2 |pages=24 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YVfHy9aFRBYC&q=Stratasys&pg=PA24 |access-date=2008-10-31}}</ref> The company is incorporated in Israel.<ref>{{cite web |title=SEC filing with information about country of incorporation |url=https://investors.stratasys.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001206774-20-000614/0001206774-20-000614.pdf |access-date=7 June 2020}}</ref> Engineers use Stratasys systems to model complex geometries in a wide range of [[polymer]] materials, including: [[Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene|ABS]], [[polyphenylsulfone]] (PPSF), [[polycarbonate]] (PC), [[polyetherimide]] and Nylon 12.

[[File:F3300_Rendering.jpg|thumb|Stratasys F3300 industrial 3D printer platform]]

Stratasys manufactures in-office prototyping and direct digital manufacturing systems for automotive, aerospace, industrial, recreational, electronic, medical and consumer product [[OEMs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.businessweek.com/hot_growth/2006/company/91.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060615032901/http://www.businessweek.com/hot_growth/2006/company/91.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 15, 2006 |title=Hot Growth Companies: Stratasys Profile |work=[[BusinessWeek]] |access-date=2008-10-31 }}</ref>

==History==
Stratasys was founded in 1989, by [[S. Scott Crump]] and his wife Lisa Crump in [[Eden Prairie, Minnesota]]. The idea for the technology came to Crump in 1988 when he decided to make a toy frog for his young daughter using a [[glue gun]] loaded with a mixture of polyethylene and [[candle]] wax. He thought of creating the shape layer by layer and of a way to automate the process. In April 1992, Stratasys sold its first product, the 3D Modeler.<ref>[http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/stratasys-inc-history/ Stratasy company history], Funding Universe</ref>

In October 1994, Stratasys had an [[initial public offering]] on [[Nasdaq]]; the company sold 1.38 million shares of [[common stock]] at $5 per share, netting approximately $5.7 million.<ref>[http://www.thefreelibrary.com/STRATASYS,+INC.+ANNOUNCES+INITIAL+PUBLIC+OFFERING+OF+1.2+MILLION...-a015825555 Stratasys, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSYS) announce an initial public offering of 1,200,000 shares of its Common Stock] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316192442/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/STRATASYS%2c+INC.+ANNOUNCES+INITIAL+PUBLIC+OFFERING+OF+1.2+MILLION...-a015825555 |date=2016-03-16 }}; PRNewswire, 20 Oct 1994</ref>

In January 1995, Stratasys purchased [[IBM]]'s [[rapid prototyping]] intellectual property and other assets and employed 16 former IBM engineers, who had been developing a small 3-D printer that relied on an [[extrusion]] system very similar to Crump's patented [[fused deposition modeling]] (FDM) technology.<ref>[http://www.thefreelibrary.com/STRATASYS+PURCHASES+IBM+RAPID+PROTOTYPING+TECHNOLOGY-a015976273 Stratasys purchases IBM's rapid prototyping technology] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305095535/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/STRATASYS+PURCHASES+IBM+RAPID+PROTOTYPING+TECHNOLOGY-a015976273 |date=2016-03-05 }}; PRNewswire, 3 Jan 1995</ref>

In 2003, Stratasys [[fused deposition modeling]] (FDM)<ref>{{cite book |title=Rapid Prototyping |author=Chee Kai Chua |author2=Kah Fai Leong |author3=Chu Sing Lim |year=2003 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-238-117-0 |pages=124 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hpNT01xw4EEC&q=Stratasys&pg=PA124 |access-date=2008-10-31}}</ref> was the best-selling rapid prototyping technology.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.forbes.com/global/2004/0920/044.html| title= Almost Out of the Woods| work=Forbes.com| access-date=2007-02-17}}</ref> FDM is a process that the company patented, which is used to produce three-dimensional parts directly from 3D [[CAD]] files layer-by-layer for use in design verification, prototyping, development and manufacturing. 

In 2007, Stratasys supplied 44% of all additive fabrication systems installed worldwide, making it the unit market leader for the sixth consecutive year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wohlers Report 2008 |last=Wohlers |first=Terry |year=2008 |publisher=Wohlers Associates |url=http://wohlersassociates.com/}}</ref>

In January 2010, Stratasys signed an agreement with [[Hewlett-Packard|HP]] to manufacture HP-branded [[3D printer]]s.<ref>[http://www.shapeways.com/blog/archives/357-stratasys-and-hp-join-forces-to-make-3d-printers.html Stratasys and HP join forces to make 3D printers]; Shapeways, January 19. 2010 </ref> In August 2012, the [[Hewlett-Packard|HP]] manufacturing and distribution agreement was discontinued.

In May 2011, Stratasys announced that they had acquired [[Solidscape]], a leader in high-precision 3D printers for lost wax casting applications.<ref >{{Cite news |title=Stratasys Acquires 3D Printer Maker, Solidscape |url=http://investors.stratasys.com/releasedetail.cfm?releaseid=599807 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111029145555/http://investors.stratasys.com/releasedetail.cfm?releaseid=599807 |archive-date=2011-10-29 |date=May 3, 2011}}</ref>

In 2012, [[Defense Distributed]], an unrelated project to produce a working firearm by 3D printing, was intended to use a Stratasys printer. Stratasys refused to permit this and withdrew its license for use of the printer, citing that it did not allow its printers "to be used for illegal purposes".<ref >{{Cite news |title=Plans to print a gun halted as 3D printer is seize |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-19813382 |date=3 October 2012 |publisher=[[BBC News Online]]}}</ref><ref name="wired">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/dangerroom/2012/10/3d-gun-blocked/  |title=3-D Printer Company Seizes Machine From Desktop Gunsmith |first=Robert
  |last=Beckhusen  |magazine=Wired |publisher=[[Wired News]] |date=2012-10-01 |access-date=2013-06-12}}</ref>

In 2014 the Israeli fashion designer [[Noa Raviv]] featured grid pattern centered couture garments which were created employing Stratasys' 3D printing technology. Some selections from the aforementioned collection were exhibited in 2016 at the exhibition "Manus X Machina" at the [[Anna Wintour Costume Center]] at [[New York City]]'s [[Metropolitan Museum of Art]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blog.stratasys.com/2014/08/28/noa-raviv-3d-printing-fashion/|title=2D Fashion Meets 3D Printing in Noa Raviv's New Award-Winning Collection|access-date=2016-08-24|archive-date=2018-08-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803195947/http://blog.stratasys.com/2014/08/28/noa-raviv-3d-printing-fashion/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dezeen.com/2014/08/21/noa-raviv-hard-copy-fashion-collection-grid-patterns-3d-printing/|title=Noa Raviv combines grid patterns and 3D printing for Hard Copy fashion collection|author=Dan Howarth|website=[[Dezeen]]|date=August 21, 2014|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref>

In 2019, the J750 model was recognized as the Enterprise 3D Printer of the Year in the polymer printer category at the 2019 3D Printing Industry Awards in London, England.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://3dprintingindustry.com/news/2019-3d-printing-industry-awards-winners-announced-156727/|title=2019 3D Printing Industry Awards winners announced|date=2019-06-11|website=3D Printing Industry|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-08}}</ref>

In May 2023, Stratasys agreed to combine with [[Desktop Metal]] in an all-stock transaction worth at $1.8{{nbsp}}billion, in which existing Stratasys shareholders will own around 59{{nbsp}}percent of the combined company.<ref name=acq>{{cite news |last1=Roof |first1=Katie |last2=Baker |first2=Liana |date=May 25, 2023 |title=Stratasys to Combine With Desktop Metal in $1.8 Billion Deal |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-05-25/stratasys-to-combine-with-desktop-metal-in-1-8-billion-deal |publisher=Bloomberg News}}</ref> Prior to, and following the acquisition announcement, Stratasys received multiple unsolicited bids to be acquired by part-owner Nano Dimensions, and in June, received another offer for $1.2{{nbsp}}billion from its competitor [[3D Systems]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Kennedy |first=Patrick |date=June 2, 2023 |title=Stratasys receives another $1B takeover bid as 3-D printer market consolidate |url=https://www.startribune.com/stratasys-receives-another-takeover-bid-as-3-d-printer-market-looks-to-consolidate-3d-systems/600279714/ |work=Star Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Heater |first=Brian |date=June 2, 2023 |title=After Stratasys and Desktop Metal announce merger plans, 3D Systems proposes acquisition |url=https://techcrunch.com/2023/06/02/after-stratasys-and-desktop-metal-announce-merger-plans-3d-systems-proposes-acquisition/ |website=TechCrunch}}</ref> Stratasys terminated the acquisition in September after its shareholders voted against the Desktop Metal acquisition as both major [[proxy advisor]]y firms [[Glass Lewis]] and [[Institutional Shareholder Services]] recommended against the deal.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Habib-Valdhorn |first=Shiri |date=September 28, 2023 |title=Stratasys shareholders nix merger with Desktop Metal |url=https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-stratasys-shareholders-nix-merger-with-desktop-metal-1001459006 |work=Globes}}</ref>

In August 2024, Stratasys filed a suit against Chinese 3D printing company [[Bambu Lab]], alleging patent infringement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sher |first=Davide |date=2024-08-10 |title=Stratasys files patent infringement lawsuit against Bambu Lab |url=https://www.voxelmatters.com/stratasys-files-patent-infringement-lawsuit-against-bambu-lab/ |access-date=2024-08-11 |website=VoxelMatters - The heart of additive manufacturing |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2025, Stratasys launched its TrueDent solution in Europe, bringing monolithic digital dentures to the regional dental market<ref>{{Cite web |title=– Company Announcement - FT.com |url=https://markets.ft.com/data/announce/detail?dockey=600-202501140815BIZWIRE_USPRX____20250114_BW856677-1 |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=markets.ft.com}}</ref>

 In March 2025, the company expanded its dental presence in Europe through new distribution agreements with Galimplant, Gold Quadrat, and Métaux Précieux <ref>{{Cite web |last=IQ |first=S&P Capital |date=2025-03-24 |title=Stratasys Ltd. Rapidly Expanding European Dental Presence with New Partners Galimplant, Gold Quadrat and Metaux Precieux {{!}} MarketScreener UK |url=https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/STRATASYS-LTD-12111547/news/Stratasys-Ltd-Rapidly-Expanding-European-Dental-Presence-with-New-Partners-Galimplant-Gold-Quadrat-49415220/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=uk.marketscreener.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> Fast Company named Stratasys one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies of 2025 for its advancements in polymer 3D printing technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chakraborty |first=Srabanti |date=2025-03-19 |title=Stratasys named to Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025 |url=https://www.engineering.com/stratasys-named-to-fast-companys-most-innovative-companies-2025/ |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Engineering.com |language=en-US}}</ref> 

===Mergers and acquisitions===
On April 16, 2012, Stratasys announced that it agreed to [[Mergers and acquisitions|merge]] with privately held [[Objet Geometries|Objet Ltd.]], a leading manufacturer of [[3D printer]]s based in [[Rehovot]], [[Israel]], in an all-stock transaction. Stratasys [[shareholders]] were expected to own 55 percent of the combined company, and Objet shareholders would own 45 percent. The merger was completed on December 3, 2012; the [[market capitalization]] of the new company was approximately $3.0 billion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/business/2012-12-05/ty-article/.premium/israeli-3d-printer-maker-merges-with-u-s-rival/0000017f-defa-df9c-a17f-fefa74ee0000|title=3D Printer Maker Objet Merges With Its U.S. Rival|author=Dror Raich, Inbal Orpaz|newspaper=[[Haaretz]]|date=December 5, 2012|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref>

On June 19, 2013, [[MakerBot Industries]] announced that it was purchased by Stratasys for $403 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/3d-printing-is-the-new-dimension-for-aerospace-industry-1.295393|title=3D printing is the new dimension for aerospace industry|author=Neil Parmar|newspaper=[[The National (Abu Dhabi)]]|date=August 6, 2013|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref>

On April 2, 2014, Stratasys announced that they had entered into definitive agreements to acquire [[Solid Concepts]] and Harvest Technologies, which will be combined with RedEye, its existing digital manufacturing service business, to establish a single additive manufacturing services business unit.<ref> [http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stratasys-to-acquire-solid-concepts-and-harvest-technologies-2014-04-02];MarketWatch, April 2, 2014 </ref> The acquisition was finalized on July 15, 2014.<ref>[https://www.cnbc.com/id/101836584] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814050802/http://www.cnbc.com/id/101836584|date=2014-08-14}}; CNBC.com, July 15, 2014</ref>

In February 2016, Stratasys announced an investment in Israeli company [[Massivit]] to promote and deploy Massivit 3D's proprietary super-sized 3D printing solutions.

On November 4, 2016, Inkbit announced that Stratasys led an equity funding round with DSM Venturing to propel production of its Vision-based, artificial intelligence additive manufacturing platform.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inkbit3d.com/press-releases/inkbit-raises-dollar12-million-in-equity-round-led-by-stratasys-and-dsm-venturing|title=Inkbit {{!}} Inkbit Raises $12 Million in Equity Round Led by Stratasys and DSM Venturing|website=inkbit3d.com|access-date=2019-11-04}}</ref>

On December 9, 2020, Stratasys announced a deal to acquire San Francisco-based Origin for $100 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stratasys to Acquire Origin, Bringing New Additive Manufacturing Platform to Polymer Production|url=https://investors.stratasys.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/717/stratasys-to-acquire-origin-bringing-new-additive|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Stratasys Ltd.|date=9 December 2020 |language=en}}</ref> The acquisition was finalized on December 31, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stratasys Completes Acquisition of Origin, Accelerating Expansion Into Mass Production Additive Manufacturing|url=https://investors.stratasys.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/721/stratasys-completes-acquisition-of-origin-accelerating|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Stratasys Ltd.|date=5 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

On April 27, 2021, Stratasys announced the Stratasys Origin One, an updated version of the Origin One 3D Printer targeted towards production applications.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stratasys Aggressively Advances Additive Manufacturing Strategy With 3D Printing Triple Play|url=https://investors.stratasys.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/736/stratasys-aggressively-advances-additive-manufacturing|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Stratasys Ltd.|date=27 April 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, Stratasys acquired the outstanding shares of Xaar 3D, which Stratasys purchased from [[Xaar plc|Xaar]]. Xaar 3D provides 3D printers using SAF Selective Absorption Fusion technology, a type of powder bed fusion. This technology is designed to 3D print polymer production parts at volume. The first printer used the technology is called the H350.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hanaphy |first1=Paul |title=Stratasys takes full control of Xaar 3D to boost high-throughput H Series 3D printing |url=https://3dprintingindustry.com/news/stratasys-takes-full-control-of-xaar-3d-to-boost-high-throughput-h-series-3d-printing-197239/ |website=3D Printing Industry |date=October 6, 2021}}</ref>

In 2021, Stratasys announced the acquisition of RP Support Ltd. (RPS), which makes large [[stereolithography]] 3D printers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stratasys acquires UK 3D printing co RP Support |url=https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-stratasys-acquires-uk-3d-printing-co-rp-support-1001361289 |website=[[Globes (newspaper)|Globes]] |date=February 18, 2021}}</ref>

On May 12, 2022, [[MakerBot]] and [[Ultimaker]] announced plans to merge. The new single company is to be backed by NPM Capital and MakerBot-owner Stratasys and co-led by existing CEOs Nadav Goshen and Jürgen von Hollen.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Heater |first1=Brian |title=MakerBot and Ultimaker announce plans to merge |url=https://techcrunch.com/2022/05/12/makerbot-and-ultimaker-are-merging/ |website=[[TechCrunch]] |date=May 12, 2022}}</ref>

In October 2022, Stratasys acquired the [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]]-headquartered quality assurance software company Riven.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Network |first=3D Printing Media |date=2022-10-26 |title=Stratasys acquires software company Riven |url=https://www.3dprintingmedia.network/stratasys-acquires-software-company-riven/ |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=3D Printing Media Network - The Pulse of the AM Industry |language=en-US}}</ref>

April 5, 2023 Stratasys Completes Acquisition of Covestro’s Additive Manufacturing Materials Business<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davies |first=Sam |date=2023-04-05 |title=Stratasys completes Covestro Additive Manufacturing acquisition |url=https://www.tctmagazine.com/api/content/41250422-d306-11ed-8312-12163087a831/ |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=TCT Magazine |language=en-gb}}</ref>

In March 2024, Stratasys acquired the intellectual property portfolio of Arevo, a Silicon Valley-based company specializing in continuous carbon fiber 3D printing.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ltd |first=Stratasys |title=Stratasys Acquires Arevo Inc.'s Intellectual Property Estate |url=https://preproduction.sme.org/technologies/articles/2024/march/stratasys-acquires-arevo-inc.s-intellectual-property-estate |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=SME |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2025, Stratasys acquired the key assets and operations of Forward AM Technologies GmbH, formerly part of BASF to expand the company's 3D printing materials portfolio.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Stratasys acquires former BASF Additive Manufacturing business Forward AM |url=https://www.metal-am.com/stratasys-acquires-former-basf-additive-manufacturing-business-forward-am/ |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=Metal Additive Manufacturing |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In July 2025, Stratasys acquired a collection of assets from Nexa3D, including Intellectual Property (IP) and equipment. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Griffiths |first=Laura |date=2025-07-07 |title=Stratasys acquires select 3D printing assets from Nexa3D |url=https://www.tctmagazine.com/api/content/fb64eb56-5b2e-11f0-9f97-1248ae80e59d/ |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=TCT Magazine |language=en-gb}}</ref>

== 3D car production systems ==

[[File:Fortus_450mc_-_Interacting.jpg|thumb|Fortus 450mc system in operational use]]

In 2014, Stratasys prototyped an electric car with fully 3D-printed exterior panels, and a few printed interior parts. Development took one year, and parts were constructed using a Stratasys Objet1000.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.stratasys.com/2014/11/18/streetscooter-3d-printing/ |title=Revolutionary New Electric Car Built and Tested in One Year with Objet1000 Multi-material 3D Production System |access-date=2014-11-24 |archive-date=2014-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129043617/http://blog.stratasys.com/2014/11/18/streetscooter-3d-printing/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Urbee===
Urbee<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130412083341/http://www.stratasys.com/resources/case-studies/automotive/urbee Stratasys 3D Printers Build Urbee, First Prototype Car to Have Entire Body Created with an Additive Process]</ref> is the first car in the world manufactured using additive manufacturing technology (its [[Car body style|bodywork]] and [[car window]]s were "printed"). Created in 2010, through a partnership with the Canadian engineering group [[KOR Ecologic]],<ref>[http://korecologic.com/ KOR Ecologic]</ref> it is a [[hybrid vehicle]] with a futuristic look.<ref>[http://www.tecmundo.com.br/impressora/6260-conheca-o-urbee-primeiro-carro-a-ser-fabricado-com-uma-impressora-3d.htm tecmundo.com.br/] ''Conheça o Urbee, primeiro carro a ser fabricado com uma impressora 3D'']</ref><ref>[http://truth-out.org/news/item/27430-the-urbee-3d-printed-car-coast-to-coast-on-10-gallons The "Urbee" 3D-Printed Car: Coast to Coast on 10 Gallons] November 23, 2014. [[Truthout]]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vI12MqoYQto 3D Printed Car Creator Discusses Future of the Urbee] YouTube</ref>
